identity.title: Pōniuā'ena: A Luminous z = 7.5 Quasar Hosting a 1.5 Billion Solar Mass Black Hole

paper_type_evidence.quote: We report the discovery of a luminous quasar, J1007+2115 at $z=7.515$ (“Pōniuā‘ena’’), from our wide-field reionization-era quasar survey.
We detect the 158 $\mu$m \[C II\] emission line in J1007+2115 with ALMA

question.value: Discover a z~7.5 quasar, measure its black hole mass, constrain early SMBH growth and the IGM neutral fraction, and get a [CII] systemic redshift and host properties with ALMA

evidence.loc: Introduction
evidence.quote: Its discovery enables new measurements of a quasar Ly$\alpha$ damping wing and provides new constraints on the earliest SMBH growth.

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~5-20 GB raw ALMA for one short Band 6 execution; NIR spectra are small
reproducibility.score_reason: The ALMA part is minimal in detail; the main results (M_BH, x_HI) rely on NIR spectra and an in-prep simulation model.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: ALMA recipe is sparse and the central results depend on non-ALMA data and unpublished models.
